issues: No integrity problems: the diff only switches to Morgan count fingerprints and generalises the Tanimoto kernel to counts. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of test labels.

The count-based Tanimoto is correct. Summing (A>=t)·(B>=t) over the thresholds t gives Σ min(a,b), and the denominator na+nb−inter with count sums gives the standard min/max (Ruzicka) similarity. The loop runs up to the largest count, which is small for Morgan fingerprints, so runtime and memory stay within limits.

Recomputed z: (0.4830−0.4804)/(0.0070·√2) ≈ 0.26 with one run on each side, which matches the harness's 0.255 within rounding. The 0.0026 gain is well inside the noise, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers. A replicate run would be needed before claiming any improvement.
Small simplicity note: the explicit threshold loop is less tidy than np.minimum-based code, but it is fine for memory and is not a reason to veto.
